entities.text: S.Shri Nakoda Agencies vs The Commissioner Of Food Safety
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1 The petitioner has come up with the present writ petition to quash the notification of the respondent, dated 23.05.2017 as illegal in so far as ''Chewing Tobacco'' is concerned and to forbear the respondent from seizing Hans Chhap Tobacco dealt by the petitioner concern.

2.Heard Mr.K.R.Laxman, learned counsel for the petitioner and Mr.G.Muthukannan, learned Government Advocate for the respondent and perused the materials available on record.
3.According to the petitioner, it is a registered proprietorship firm with GST Registration of Government of India and Government of Tamil Nadu and it is dealing with tobacco produces since 2016 with prior licenses obtained and without violating any provision of law.
4.Mr

entities.text: GST Registration of Government of India
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: .G.Muthukannan, learned Government Advocate for the respondent would submit that the 1st respondent has rightly passed the impugned order and there is no illegality in the order passed by the respondent.

5.By the impugned notification, the respondent initiated proceedings against the petitioner for violation of provision of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and the Food Safety and Standards (Prohibition and Restrictions on Sales) Regulations, 2011.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards (Prohibition and Restrictions on Sales) Regulations, 2011
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The notification is challenged by the petitioner mainly contending that since he is the dealer of TOBACCO protects, the provisions referred in the notification have no application.
6.It is not in dispute that the issue involved in this Writ Petition is covered by the order of this Court passed in W.P.No.21 of 2017, dated 09.06.2017.
7.Following the said order, the order impugned, dated 23.05.2017, in the Writ Petition is set aside and the Writ Petition is allowed.
No costs.
Consequently, consequently Miscellaneous Petitions are closed.
However, it is made clear that this order will not stand in the way the appropriate authority to take action under COTA (Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products Act, 2003).
